_note: Life events. Each arrives as a call, text or moment in the dressing room, with choices that cost something. Effects: honour, manager, teammates, fans, family, money, energy, slot (takes your day this week), flag (remembered), unflag. 'next' queues a follow-up {id, in: weeks, chance}. 'news' puts a story in Monday's paper: page front|back, headline with {NAME}. Conditions: minWeek, notPreseason, needFlag, notFlag, meter minimums (min) / maximums (max), contract types (types), weight. Design rule: the bad choice is always tempting. Age rule: anything about the player's car or driving needs minAgeYears 18 and needFlag 'canDrive' (set by the driving lessons in the shop); pubs, nightclubs, alcohol and casinos need minAgeYears 18.

events.text: Mate. Overslept. Again. If the gaffer asks, tell him I was with you at the physio. You're a legend. Owe you one. Gaz

choices.label: Cover for him
choices.result: Gaz owes you one. Gaz has owed everyone one since 2019.

choices.label: Tell him to sort himself out
choices.result: Gaz calls you a grass in the group chat. Then sends a sad face.

events.text: Funny thing, son. The physio was in Tenerife last Tuesday. So where were you and Gaz? Think carefully. My dog can smell a sausage roll through two doors, and I can smell a lie through three.

choices.label: Come clean
choices.result: The gaffer nods slowly. Gaz runs laps until his legs are spaghetti.

choices.label: Double down on the lie
choices.result: The gaffer's eyes narrow. You've been dropped into his bad books, and the bad books are wet.

news.headline: {NAME} IN PHYSIO PORKIE PROBE

events.text: Quick one, pet. Are you starting Saturday? Only Maureen at bingo reckons you're on the bench and there's good money riding on it. Just a little nod. Nobody would know.

choices.label: Give her a little nod
choices.result: Gran makes a noise like a kettle. 'You're a good boy.'

choices.label: Gran, I can't tell you that
choices.result: 'Your grandad would've told me,' she says. Your grandad was banned from three bookmakers.

events.text: They've BANNED me from the bookies! Said my bets were 'statistically improbable'. I said I'm just lucky. They've sent a letter to the FA. Is that bad?

choices.label: Ring the FA and explain
choices.result: A tired man at the FA writes 'GRAN' on a Post-it and sighs.

news.headline: GRANNY GAMBLE: {NAME}'S NAN IN BETTING BAN

choices.label: Lie low and hope it goes away
choices.result: It doesn't go away. It never goes away.

news.headline: BETTING GRAN SHOCK: {NAME} 'KNEW NOTHING'

events.text: Hi! We'd love you to visit the children's ward on Thursday. Bring a smile and some signed photos. (Gaz says the lads are going to Wetherspoons that night. Ignore Gaz.)

choices.label: Visit the hospital (takes your day)
choices.result: A seven-year-old beats you at FIFA and tells you you're rubbish. Best afternoon of your life.

news.headline: HEARTS OF GOLD: {NAME} CHEERS SICK KIDS

choices.label: Go out with the lads
choices.result: Somebody orders a round of Jägerbombs at 6pm. It's a long night.

events.text: Sid Scoop, Weekly Splash. I've got a photo of you asleep in a kebab shop wearing a traffic cone. Any comment before we go to print?

choices.label: 'It was a fancy dress thing'
choices.result: It was not a fancy dress thing.

news.headline: CONE-HEAD! {NAME} IN KEBAB SHOP KIP

choices.label: Apologise to the club
choices.result: The gaffer accepts. He's seen worse. He did worse.

news.headline: SORRY SEEMS TO BE THE HARDEST WORD FOR CONE-HEAD {NAME}

events.text: You're live on Radio Bantam's Football Phone-In! Caller from Dudley says the gaffer's tactics are 'like watching paint dry, but the paint's also asleep'. Do you agree?

choices.label: Back the gaffer
choices.result: The gaffer texts you a single traffic cone emoji. From him, that's a hug.

choices.label: 'He's got a point, to be fair'
choices.result: The phone-in lines light up. So does the gaffer's face.

news.headline: {NAME} STICKS THE BOOT INTO GAFFER

choices.label: Talk about the gaffer's allotment for ten minutes
choices.result: You do eight minutes on his marrows. The presenter cuts to the travel news. The gaffer loved it.

events.text: It's my birthday dinner Wednesday love. Your auntie Carol's coming. She's bringing the trifle. Please come. The coach mentioned extra shooting practice though didn't he?

choices.label: Go to Mum's dinner (takes your day)
choices.result: Auntie Carol's trifle is 40% custard and 60% mystery. Mum cries twice. Lovely evening.

choices.label: Stay for extra shooting
choices.result: Mum says it's fine. It is not fine. Auntie Carol posts about it on Facebook.

events.text: Initiation night. Everyone's chanting your name. You have to stand on a chair and sing. The senior pros are watching. Gaz is filming.

choices.label: Belt out Mr Brightside
choices.result: You miss every high note. The dressing room goes wild. Gaz's video gets 40 views, all Gaz.

choices.label: Refuse, you're not a performing seal
choices.result: Silence. Someone fills your boots with yoghurt the next morning.

events.text: Hi, Nikey Sports here (not that one). We'll give you £600 to wear our boots. They're nearly leather. The swoosh goes the other way. Interested?

choices.label: Take the £600
choices.result: The boots squeak. Every step sounds like a duck being sat on.

news.headline: JUST DON'T DO IT: {NAME}'S KNOCK-OFF BOOT DEAL

choices.label: No thanks
choices.result: 'Your loss,' they text. Then: 'Would you do it for £400?'

events.text: You're in the big Shopco in your pyjama bottoms buying Coco Pops when a fan spots you. 'Can I get a selfie? And can you do a video for my brother? He hates you.'

choices.label: Smile, selfie, video, the lot
choices.result: The brother still hates you, but he hates you a bit less.

choices.label: Pretend you're someone else
choices.result: 'You're definitely him,' she says. 'You've got his face.'

news.headline: PYJAMA DRAMA: {NAME} SNUBS FAN IN CEREAL AISLE

events.text: Son. I'm down the allotment Sunday. Dawn start. Bring a flask and a spade. Don't tell the others, they'll want to come and they dig like idiots.

choices.label: Dig the allotment with the gaffer (takes your day)
choices.result: Six hours. One marrow. He names it after you and enters it in the village show. It's the happiest you've ever seen him.

choices.label: Make an excuse
choices.result: 'Suit yourself,' he says, in the voice of a man who will remember this.

events.text: Big Terry, club captain, 34, has taken your peg, your towel and your protein shake. 'Rookies get the corner by the bin,' he says. The lads are watching.

choices.label: Stand up to him
choices.result: Big Terry stares at you for a long time. Then he laughs and gives you the towel back. The shake's gone though.

choices.label: Corner by the bin it is
choices.result: It's not too bad by the bin. You get to know the bin quite well.

events.text: Oi superstar. The Red Lion are in the cup final Sunday and we're short. Come on, one game, for old times. Ref's blind. Pitch is a swamp. You'll love it.

choices.label: Play for the Red Lion (takes your day)
choices.result: You score a hat-trick in wellies. Deano cries. You're banned from the Red Lion's car park for life (long story).

choices.label: Can't risk the injury, sorry
choices.result: Deano sends a voice note. It's just him saying 'Big time Charlie' for forty seconds.

events.text: Someone's sent me a video of you in a Red Lion shirt, on a swamp, doing a knee slide into a dog. Explain.

choices.label: 'It was for charity'
choices.result: 'Which charity?' 'The Red Lion.' Long silence.

news.headline: PUB-LIC ENEMY: {NAME} RISKS IT ALL IN SUNDAY LEAGUE

choices.label: Hold your hands up
choices.result: He fines you a week's tea money. Fair.

events.text: Bro can I borrow £500. Car's failed its MOT and I need it for, er, a car thing. Pay you back next week 100%. Kev

choices.label: Lend him £500
choices.result: Kev hugs you so hard your back clicks.

choices.label: Sorry Kev, skint
choices.result: Kev says no worries. Kev is very worried.

events.text: Told you bro! £500 back plus a Twix for interest. Legend.

choices.label: Accept the Twix
choices.result: Best interest rate you'll ever get.

events.text: The prank war's escalated. Somebody's put cling film over the gaffer's toilet. Everyone thinks it was you. It wasn't. Was it?

choices.label: Go bigger: fill Gaz's car with balloons
choices.result: Four hundred balloons. Gaz opens the door and becomes a viral sensation.

news.headline: POP IDOL: {NAME}'S BALLOON BUST-UP

choices.label: Stay well out of it
choices.result: You eat your lunch alone, but with dignity.

events.text: Dear former pupil. We'd love you to present the prizes at Prize Day. Mr Hargreaves (PE) says he 'always knew'. He did not always know.

choices.label: Present the prizes (takes your day)
choices.result: Mr Hargreaves calls you 'my lad'. Your old maths teacher asks for a selfie. Revenge tastes like Ribena.

news.headline: HEAD OF THE CLASS: {NAME} BACK AT SCHOOL

choices.label: Too busy, sorry
choices.result: They get the local weatherman instead. He's thrilled.

events.text: Sid Scoop. I'll write you a lovely puff piece. 'Wonderkid', the works. All I need is the team for Saturday. Who's playing? Tiny thing. Nobody gets hurt.

choices.label: Leak the team
choices.result: Sid sends you £200 in an envelope that smells of pickled onions.

news.headline: WONDERKID {NAME}: THE NEXT BIG THING?

choices.label: Tell Sid where to go
choices.result: 'You'll regret that,' says Sid. You suspect he's right.

events.text: Somebody leaked my team to Sid Scoop. I've narrowed it down to you, Gaz and the bloke who does the pies. The pie bloke can't read. And Gaz can't spell 'team'.

choices.label: Confess
choices.result: He doesn't shout. That's worse. He just sighs, like a slow puncture.

choices.label: Blame the pie bloke
choices.result: The pie bloke is sacked. The pies are worse now. Everyone knows.

events.text: I won again on you, pet! I've bought you a present. It's a gold chain. It's very big. It says your name. In diamonds. Well, nearly diamonds.

choices.label: Wear it with pride
choices.result: It weighs more than your boots. The lads call you Mr T.

news.headline: BLING IT ON: {NAME}'S GRAN GOES FOR GOLD

choices.label: Thank her, hide it in a drawer
choices.result: Gran checks every photo of you for the chain. Every. Photo.

events.text: Love, the club nutritionist rang. She says you've been living on Pot Noodles. I've booked you a cooking class with Auntie Carol. Thursday. It's non-negotiable. x

choices.label: Go to the cooking class (takes your day)
choices.result: You learn three meals. Two involve tinned peaches.

choices.label: Order a Deliveroo instead
choices.result: Your Deliveroo rider recognises you and asks why you're always ordering chicken nuggets at 11pm.

events.text: Congratulations! You've been voted Supporters' Player of the Month! The award ceremony is at the Working Men's Club. There'll be a buffet. A big one.

choices.label: Go and give a speech
choices.result: You thank your mum, your gran and the buffet. Standing ovation.

news.headline: FANS' FAVOURITE: {NAME} SCOOPS MONTHLY GONG

choices.label: Send a video message
choices.result: The video plays sideways. Everyone watches it sideways.

events.text: A bloke in the car park shouts 'Get a proper striker!' at you. His mate shouts 'Or a proper haircut!' Then they ask for an autograph for their kid.

choices.label: Sign it, and smile
choices.result: 'You're alright, you,' says the first bloke. Progress.

choices.label: Tell them what you think of them
choices.result: Someone films it. It's not your best angle.

news.headline: CAR PARK CLASH: {NAME} BLOWS HIS TOP

events.text: Tony here. Super-agent. Lunch. My treat. Steakhouse. I've got contacts in Dubai, Madrid and a bloke in Rhyl. Sign nothing, just eat.

choices.label: Go to lunch
choices.result: Tony orders for you, takes a photo of you, and leaves you with the bill. £180.

choices.label: Ignore him
choices.result: Tony sends you 14 voice notes. One is just him chewing.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Funny photo landed on my desk: you, a steakhouse, and Tony 'Ten Percent' Malone. Are you leaving the club?

choices.label: 'No comment'
choices.result: 'No comment' means yes in newspaper.

news.headline: STEAK-OUT: {NAME} IN SECRET AGENT LUNCH

choices.label: 'I love this club'
choices.result: Sid prints it anyway, with a photo of you holding a steak knife.

news.headline: {NAME}: I'M NOT GOING ANYWHERE (PROBABLY)

events.text: Dennis grabs your arm in the corridor. 'Tuesday. A seagull. Don't eat the sausage roll.' He walks off. On Tuesday a seagull steals your sausage roll. Dennis winks at you from across the car park.

choices.label: Ask Dennis what else he knows
choices.result: 'You'll be famous,' he says. 'Or infamous. Depends on the slippers.' What slippers?

choices.label: Back away slowly
choices.result: You start checking for seagulls everywhere. There are always seagulls.

events.text: Mate. Hear me out. Vape shop. For DOGS. Flavours: bacon, postman, next door's cat. I just need £500 to get started. You'll get 20%. Of the profits. Of the dogs.

choices.label: Invest £500
choices.result: Deano cries. He promises you'll be 'on the ground floor'. The ground floor is his mum's garage.

choices.label: Not a chance
choices.result: Deano says you've 'changed'. You have. You've learned what a dog vape is.

events.text: Dog vapes didn't work (RSPCA got involved). BUT. Novelty slippers. Shaped like YOUR face. Fans will go mad. I've found a supplier. Minimum order 40,000. I need £5,000. This is the one.

choices.label: Back him with £5,000
choices.result: Somewhere in China, a factory starts making 40,000 of your face.

choices.label: Absolutely not
choices.result: Deano finds another investor. It's his nan. Dennis the kit man looks relieved.

events.text: Slight problem. The slippers arrived. They've got your face on, but it's not really your face. It's more like a sad potato. Nobody's buying. They're in your garage. All of them. Also the press know.

choices.label: Laugh it off and sign a few for charity
choices.result: A children's hospital gets 500 signed potato slippers. The kids love them. Deano sells the rest at a car boot for 20p each.

news.headline: STRIKER'S 40,000 SLIPPERS SHAME

choices.label: Blame Deano in public
choices.result: Deano unfollows you. Then refollows you to unfollow you again, so you notice.

news.headline: SLIPPER-Y SLOPE: {NAME} DUMPS BEST MATE OVER 40,000 FACE SLIPPERS

events.text: PARTY AT MINE SATURDAY 🎉🎉 foam machine CONFIRMED. bring the lads. bring snacks. bring a towel (foam).

choices.label: Go (but leave early, match day)
choices.result: You leave at 10pm. Shaz calls you 'grandad' in the group chat. Worth it.

choices.label: Go all in
choices.result: You wake up covered in foam on a sun lounger. It's Sunday. It might be Monday.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Lovely photos from a foam party. You, a sun lounger, a traffic cone (again), and what looks like a goat. Comment?

choices.label: 'The goat was invited'
choices.result: The goat becomes a minor celebrity.

news.headline: FOAM-ALITY: {NAME} AND THE PARTY GOAT

choices.label: Ask Shaz to make a statement
choices.result: Shaz's statement is a 40-second voice note of her laughing.

news.headline: BUBBLE TROUBLE FOR {NAME}

events.text: Got a van full of tellies. Don't ask. 75-inch. Hundred quid each. You want one? Your mum wants one. I've already asked your mum.

choices.label: Take a telly (£100)
choices.result: It's a great telly. It has someone else's Netflix logged in.

choices.label: Lee, I can't
choices.result: 'Your loss,' says Lee. 'Ninety quid?'

events.text: Card night at mine Friday. Proper game. Bring cash. My cousin Tel's playing. Don't stare at Tel's eyebrow.

choices.label: I'm in (opens Big Lee's card nights in the Casino)
choices.result: Tel's eyebrow is mesmerising. Big Lee's card nights are now in your Casino menu.

choices.label: Not for me
choices.result: Lee says 'suit yourself' and deals Tel in.

events.text: bro. BRO. need u on my new track. just say 'big ting' 4 times in a deep voice. gonna be massive. trust.

choices.label: Record it
choices.result: The track gets 40,000 plays. 39,000 are people laughing at you. You're a meme. A popular meme.

news.headline: BIG TING ENERGY: {NAME}'S RAP DEBUT

choices.label: Leave me out of it
choices.result: Ty goes quiet. Ty is never quiet.

events.text: dropped a diss track about u. its called 'Bench Warmer'. no hard feelings. its fire tho.

choices.label: Respond with a diss track of your own
choices.result: Your track rhymes 'bench' with 'bench'. The internet decides you've won anyway.

news.headline: RAP BEEF: {NAME} BITES BACK

choices.label: Rise above it
choices.result: Ty's track gets 600 plays. He blames the algorithm.

events.text: I looked at your bank statement (you left it open). You spent £84 on Greggs last week. EIGHTY FOUR. Let me set you up with a savings plan. I'll do it for free. Well, for a sausage roll.

choices.label: Let Priya sort it
choices.result: Priya puts £200 in your rainy day fund and bans you from Greggs on weekdays.

choices.label: I'm fine, honestly
choices.result: You buy a sausage roll to prove a point. It is not a point.

events.text: Grown-up talk: rent is money you never see again. If you buy somewhere sensible, it's an investment. Not a moat. Please don't buy a moat.

choices.label: Listen. Properly.
choices.result: Priya draws a graph. You understand 60% of it. That's 60% more than your agent.

choices.label: 'What about a moat though?'
choices.result: Priya puts her head on the table for a long time.

events.text: Watched your last game. Your left hamstring's tight, you're landing heavy on it. Come round, I'll sort you a routine. Free. I need the practice and you need the hamstring.

choices.label: Go round (takes your day)
choices.result: Mo's routine is mostly lying on the floor groaning. You feel brand new.

choices.label: It's fine, I'll stretch
choices.result: You don't stretch.

events.text: The youth club roof's leaking again. We're doing a sponsored penalty shoot-out. Would you go in goal? The kids want to score past a 'real footballer'. Even a striker.

choices.label: Go in goal (takes your day)
choices.result: You let in 112 penalties. They raise £2,300. The roof gets fixed. A seven-year-old does a Cristiano celebration in your face.

news.headline: SAVE OF THE DAY: {NAME} LETS IN 112 FOR CHARITY

choices.label: Send a signed shirt
choices.result: The shirt raises £40. It's a nice shirt.

events.text: Son. A word from an old pro. The game'll chew you up if you let it. Look after your mum, save your money, and never trust a man in a long coat who says 'trust me'. That's all. Oh, and wear long studs.

choices.label: Thank him, properly
choices.result: Stan goes quiet, then says 'your grandad would've been proud'. You both pretend you've got something in your eye.

choices.label: 'Cheers Stan' (you're busy)
choices.result: Stan says 'right you are' and tells the same thing to the man in the newsagent.

events.text: We need to talk. You're never here. When you are here, you're watching yourself on Match of the Day. I think we're done.

choices.label: Beg for one more chance (takes your day)
choices.result: A long walk, a longer talk, and a chippy tea. You're still together. Just.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.result: It's over. Mum brings round a lasagne. Gran says 'plenty more fish', then 'your grandad would've said that'.

news.headline: HEARTBREAK FOR {NAME}: IT'S OVER

events.text: They're brushing their teeth at yours. Again. 'I've basically moved in,' they say. 'Shall we make it official?'

choices.label: Move in together
choices.result: Their stuff arrives. So does a ferret. Nobody mentioned a ferret.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: 'Fine,' they say. It is not fine. They take their toothbrush home pointedly.

events.text: You've got the ring. It's been in your sock drawer for three weeks. Gran knows. Dennis knows. Somehow Sid Scoop knows. It's now or never.

choices.label: Get down on one knee
choices.result: They say yes before you've finished the question. You were going to say a whole poem.

news.headline: DOWN ON ONE KNEE: {NAME} POPS THE QUESTION

choices.label: Bottle it
choices.result: The ring goes back in the sock. The sock knows.

events.text: The wedding. Big do at a stately home with a swan ice sculpture and the whole squad? Or the registry office and a pub lunch?

choices.label: Big do (£40,000)
choices.result: The swan melts by 3pm. Gaz catches the bouquet. Gran wins £200 on the length of the best man's speech.

news.headline: I DO! {NAME}'S SWAN-TASTIC WEDDING

choices.label: Registry office and the Red Lion
choices.result: Deano does the speech. It's mostly about dog vapes. Perfect.

news.headline: {NAME} WEDS IN SECRET PUB DO

events.text: 3am. A stunning stranger in the VIP bit is laughing at all your jokes, even the one about the dog vapes. 'Come back to mine?' Your partner thinks you're at Gaz's.

choices.label: Go back to theirs
choices.result: It's exciting. Then it's 9am and you feel sick, and not from the Jägerbombs.

choices.label: Get a taxi home
choices.result: You're home by 3.30. Your partner's asleep with the ferret. You've never been happier.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Got photos of you leaving a flat at 9am in last night's clothes. Not your flat. Not your partner's flat. Story runs Monday. Comment?

choices.label: Tell your partner before the paper does
choices.result: There's a lot of shouting. Some crying. The ferret takes their side.

news.headline: LOVE RAT {NAME} IN 9AM WALK OF SHAME

choices.label: Deny everything
choices.result: The photos are very clear. You are very not clear.

news.headline: LIAR, LIAR: CHEAT {NAME}'S DENIAL IN TATTERS

events.text: Your new teammates keep laughing at something you said in training. The interpreter explains: you've been calling the gaffer 'my little cabbage' all week.

choices.label: Book language lessons (takes your day)
choices.result: Three weeks later you can order a coffee, apologise to the gaffer, and swear fluently. In that order.

choices.label: Keep smiling and nodding
choices.result: You agree to a lot of things. One of them, it turns out, was carrying the kit bags until Christmas.

events.text: Are you eating, love? I've posted you a box: PG Tips, Branston, a Greggs steak bake (it might not survive) and a photo of the dog. Your Gran says the foreign food will make you soft.

choices.label: Video call for an hour
choices.result: The dog licks the screen. You cry a bit. Nobody needs to know.

choices.label: Too busy, text her later
choices.result: The steak bake arrives three weeks later. It has become a different substance.

events.text: A local journalist asks, through a translator, whether you prefer it here or back home. The whole city will read the answer.

choices.label: 'I love it here, this is my home now'
choices.result: The city loves you. Your mum reads it on Google Translate and goes quiet for a day.

choices.label: 'Nothing beats a rainy Tuesday in England'
choices.result: The headline translates roughly as 'ENGLISHMAN SAYS OUR WEATHER IS BAD'. Which, to be fair, it isn't.

events.text: Mate. Tiny favour. Get yourself booked in the first ten minutes Saturday. That's it. A little yellow card. My cousin's got a bet on. £5,000 in your hand. Nobody gets hurt. It's a yellow card.

choices.label: Take the £5,000
choices.result: Lee gives you an envelope in a Greggs bag. You get booked for a 'clumsy challenge' in the seventh minute. Your heart is going like the clappers.

choices.label: Absolutely not
choices.result: Lee laughs it off. 'Only joking.' He wasn't joking.

events.text: That went beautiful. Now my cousin's mate wants something bigger. Miss a penalty. Just one. £20,000. You're in it now, son. Be a shame if anyone found out about the yellow card.

choices.label: Do it (£20,000)
choices.result: You blaze it over the bar. The crowd groans. You feel sick for a week.

choices.label: Go to the FA yourself
choices.result: The FA thank you for your honesty. You get a six-week ban for the yellow card. Lee stops speaking to you. The papers call you 'the whistleblower'.

news.headline: WHISTLEBLOWER {NAME} SHOPS BETTING GANG

events.text: The FA's integrity unit would like a word about some unusual betting patterns. On you. A yellow card and a penalty. They have phone records. And a Greggs bag.

choices.label: Confess everything
choices.result: A ten-month ban. Your name is mud. But it's over, and you told the truth.

news.headline: SHAME OF {NAME}: STRIKER BANNED FOR MATCH FIXING

choices.label: Deny it
choices.result: Your lawyer says 'it'll be fine'. It is not fine.

events.text: Guilty. Conspiracy to defraud. The judge looks at you over her glasses: 'You had everything, and you threw it away for a Greggs bag.' Eighteen months, out in nine.

choices.label: Go down quietly
choices.result: Prison is a chapter, not the end. You'll be out in nine months. Then the hard part starts.

news.headline: JAILED: {NAME} GETS 18 MONTHS FOR FIXING

events.text: VIP offer for our favourite customer! £20,000 credit line, no checks, no questions. Win it all back this weekend!

choices.label: Take the credit
choices.result: It feels like free money. It isn't free and it isn't money.

choices.label: Delete the app
choices.result: You delete it. Then you delete the other three. Priya is very proud.

events.text: The odds on your team losing Saturday are 4/1. You're owed £24,000. You know the team news. One bet would clear it all.

choices.label: Place the bet
choices.result: You win. Then the FA's systems flag it within the hour.

news.headline: {NAME} BET AGAINST OWN TEAM: FA BAN

choices.label: Get help instead
choices.result: You ring a gambling helpline at 2am. A woman called Pat talks to you for an hour. You owe Pat everything.

events.from: A man in a long coat
events.text: I represent a much bigger club. I can't say which. It rhymes with 'Smarsenal'. We'd love a quiet coffee. Nobody needs to know.

choices.label: Take the meeting quietly
choices.result: The coffee is lovely. The offer is lovelier. You leave by the back door, like a spy.

choices.label: Report it to your club
choices.result: The chairman is touched. He gives you a framed photo of himself. You didn't want it.

choices.label: Leak it to force a move
choices.result: It's on every back page by Thursday. The fans burn a replica shirt. It doesn't burn well (polyester).

news.headline: GET ME OUT: {NAME} WANTS BIG MOVE

events.text: Sid Scoop. Lovely photo of you leaving a coffee shop by the back door. With a man in a long coat. Fancy explaining?

choices.label: 'I was buying a coffee'
choices.result: Nobody believes you. Not even the barista.

news.headline: TAPPED UP! {NAME} IN SECRET COFFEE SUMMIT

choices.label: Come clean to the gaffer
choices.result: He sighs. 'Everyone's got a price, son. Just don't make me find out from Sid Scoop next time.'

events.text: Gaz's other half has had a few. She's been flirting with you all night, and now she's suggesting you 'get some air' together. Gaz is in the kitchen doing his dance.

choices.label: Get some air together
choices.result: It's a bad idea and you both know it. You do it anyway.

choices.label: Find Gaz and go and dance badly
choices.result: You and Gaz dance until 3am. It's horrific. It's the right choice.

events.text: Gaz knows. Everyone knows. Nobody's passing to you in training. Gaz threw a boot at you. Then the other boot.

choices.label: Apologise to Gaz in front of everyone
choices.result: He doesn't accept it. But the lads respect that you stood there and took it.

news.headline: LOVE RAT {NAME}: AFFAIR WITH TEAMMATE'S PARTNER

choices.label: Ask for a transfer
choices.result: The dressing room has collapsed. The gaffer has locked himself in his office with his ukulele and isn't answering. You can hear him playing something sad.

news.headline: DRESSING ROOM WAR: {NAME} AFFAIR SHAME

events.text: The forehead's winning. Gaz has started calling you 'The Moon'. A clinic in Istanbul does a package: flights, hotel, 4,000 grafts and a bandana. £6,000.

choices.label: Book the flights
choices.result: Six weeks in a bandana. Then: hair! Actual hair! Gaz has to find a new nickname.

choices.label: Shave it all off and own it
choices.result: You look like a Bond villain. A handsome one. Your partner approves.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Funny photo: you, an airport, a bandana. Want to tell the nation about your 'holiday'?

choices.label: 'Yes, I had a hair transplant. Look at it!'
choices.result: The honesty goes down a storm. The clinic sends you a fruit basket.

news.headline: HAIR TODAY: {NAME} COMES CLEAN OVER TURKEY TRANSPLANT

choices.label: 'It's a new conditioner'
choices.result: The internet zooms in on your scalp. The internet is merciless.

news.headline: BALD-FACED LIE: {NAME}'S 'CONDITIONER' CLAIM

events.text: They hand you a little stick with two lines on it. 'So,' they say. 'That happened.'

choices.label: Cry happy tears
choices.result: You both cry. Then you ring your mum. Then she cries. Then Gran puts a bet on the name.

choices.label: Panic, then cry happy tears
choices.result: You go white, sit down, stand up, sit down, then hug them for ten minutes.

events.text: "Dad, you missed my birthday. Mum said you were at training. It's fine. Grandma made the cake."

choices.label: Drive over with a present right now (takes your day)
choices.result: You arrive at bedtime with a remote-control dinosaur. Best day ever, apparently.

choices.label: Promise you'll make it next year
choices.result: "OK." The worst word in the English language.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Rupert Fox MP has been caught claiming a duck house on expenses. A gold one. You campaigned with him last month. Comment?

choices.label: 'I was wrong to back him'
choices.result: Short, sharp, done. The story moves on in a day.

news.headline: {NAME} DUCKS OUT OF FOX ROW

choices.label: 'He's a good man, I stand by him'
choices.result: Then the second duck house comes out.

news.headline: DUCK HOUSE SHAME: {NAME} STANDS BY DISGRACED MP

events.text: Dennis has lost one sock from every pair in the squad. He says the washing machine 'takes a tithe'. He's offering you a replacement pair: one is pink, one has a reindeer on it.

choices.label: Wear them with pride
choices.result: You score a screamer in training. By Friday the whole squad demands odd socks. Dennis is hailed as a prophet.

choices.label: Complain to the gaffer
choices.result: The gaffer opens an inquiry. Dennis is cleared. The washing machine is not.

events.text: A scruffy ginger cat has moved into the home dugout. It sits on the gaffer's clipboard and hisses at the goalkeeping coach. The lads want to keep it.

choices.label: Adopt it as the unofficial club cat
choices.result: You name it Tiddles. It immediately bites you. It's a perfect fit.

news.headline: PURR-FECT SIGNING: {NAME} ADOPTS TRAINING GROUND MOGGY

choices.label: Ring the animal rescue
choices.result: A nice lady takes it away. It's back by Thursday, sitting on your boots. It has chosen you.

choices.label: Feed it your protein bar
choices.result: It eats the protein bar, then your shin pad, then looks at you as if you're next.

events.text: OMG the training ground cat has 80k followers?? We want to give it an official squad number and a tiny shirt. Can you hold it for the photo? It only scratches people it respects.

choices.label: Hold the cat (and your nerve)
choices.result: The cat's tiny shirt outsells yours in the club shop by Tuesday. You have the scratches to prove you were there.

news.headline: CAT-ASTROPHE FOR {NAME} AS MOGGY OUTSELLS STRIKER

choices.label: 'It's a cat'
choices.result: The comments call you 'anti-cat'. You get a strongly worded letter from a woman in Kent with eleven of them.

events.text: Derby week. Your neighbour, a lifelong fan of the lot across town, has painted his wheelie bins in their colours and pointed them at your front window.

choices.label: Paint your bins back, twice as bright
choices.result: The street splits down the middle. The binmen refuse to collect either side.

news.headline: BIN WARS: {NAME} IN DERBY WHEELIE ROW

choices.label: Bake him a cake in your colours
choices.result: He eats the whole cake. He keeps the bins. A kind of respect has been reached.

choices.label: Ignore the bins
choices.result: The bins stay. You could swear they've started watching you.

events.text: Barry the Badger, the club mascot, has been told off for dancing in front of the away end. He wants you to 'say something' to the board. Inside the costume, Barry is a 58-year-old called Neville.

choices.label: Back Neville in public
choices.result: The board backs down. Neville celebrates with a dance so aggressive the away end applauds.

news.headline: BADGER BADGERING: {NAME} BACKS MASCOT IN BOARDROOM BUST-UP

choices.label: Stay out of badger politics
choices.result: Neville sulks. A sulking six-foot badger is a terrible thing to see on a Saturday.

events.text: Emergency! It's the half-time mascot race and we're one short. Could you wear the spare costume? It's a giant sausage roll. It smells a bit. It smells a lot, actually.

choices.label: Be the sausage roll (takes your day)
choices.result: You lead until the last ten yards, when a giant carrot takes you out with a shoulder barge. The crowd chants your name. Your pastry name.

news.headline: SAUSAGE ROLL {NAME} PIPPED BY GIANT CARROT

choices.label: Claim you've got a tight hamstring
choices.result: The costume goes to Gaz. Gaz wins. Gaz will never, ever stop talking about it.

events.text: A man with a ring binder of 900 signed photos is waiting at the training ground gate. He'd like you to sign eleven. 'For my collection.' He has a lot of collections.

choices.label: Sign all eleven
choices.result: A week later they're on an auction site. You go for £2.40 each. You're secretly quite pleased.

choices.label: Sign one, for his kid
choices.result: He doesn't have a kid. He admits it. You both laugh, nervously, then he asks for ten more.

choices.label: Sneak out the back way
choices.result: He's at the back way. He's always at the back way. He knows the back way better than you do.

events.text: HIYA!! It's the big school reunion next Friday!! Everyone's coming. I'm doing a slideshow. Yes, THAT photo is in it. Can't wait xx

choices.label: Go along (takes your day)
choices.result: The slideshow features you dressed as a pumpkin in Year 4. You get a round of applause and a pumpkin emoji from everyone for a month.

choices.label: Send apologies
choices.result: Kayleigh posts the pumpkin photo online anyway. It gets 4,000 likes. You are, forever, the pumpkin.

events.text: The club shop's new mannequin is meant to be you. It's got your shirt, your boots and somebody else's face. Possibly a weather presenter's.

choices.label: Pose with your plastic twin
choices.result: Fans queue to have their photo taken with both of you. Most of them prefer the mannequin.

news.headline: DUMMY RUN: {NAME} MEETS HIS PLASTIC TWIN

choices.label: Ask them to fix the face
choices.result: They fix it. It now looks like a startled pigeon. Everyone agrees it's an improvement.

events.text: Hi! We're short-staffed Saturday morning. Could you do an hour on the till? Customers love it. Please don't touch the scarf display, it's load-bearing.

choices.label: Work the till (takes your day)
choices.result: You sell 140 shirts with your name on. You also give a man £50 change for a keyring. He doesn't mention it. Nobody mentions it.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.result: They put up a cardboard cut-out of you instead. It shifts more stock than you would have.

events.text: Hiya!! We're doing a video where players try to say the club motto with a mouth full of crackers. It's going to be HUGE. You're up in ten mins. Don't be weird about it.

choices.label: Fill your boots (with crackers)
choices.result: You inhale a cracker. The video gets two million views. Most of it is you coughing and Kev hitting your back.

choices.label: Suggest something more dignified
choices.result: They film you reading a poem about the club. It gets 41 views. The gaffer watched it twice.

events.text: So. Slight problem. Someone posted from YOUR account at 3am. It says 'honestly i love cheese more than football'. We think it was the work experience lad. It's trending.

choices.label: Own it: post a photo hugging a wheel of cheddar
choices.result: A local dairy sends you a 20kg cheese. Your fridge will never be the same.

news.headline: SAY CHEESE: {NAME}'S CHEDDAR CONFESSION

choices.label: Demand they delete it
choices.result: It's deleted. The screenshots live forever. Away fans bring cheese to the next game.

events.text: Mick here, Big Mick's Motors! We'd love to sponsor you with a lovely little hatchback. It's got your face on the bonnet. And mine on the roof. Mine's bigger. Interested?

choices.label: Take the car and the cash
choices.result: Everyone can see you coming for half a mile. Mick waves at you from the roof at every roundabout.

news.headline: FACE THE FACTS: {NAME}'S BONNET BONANZA

choices.label: No thanks, Mick
choices.result: Mick gives the deal to the club mascot. Barry the Badger now drives a car with his face on it.

events.text: Hello from Spudz Crisps! We'd like you to be the face of our bold new flavour: Prawn Custard. You'll have to eat them on camera. Quite a lot of them. With a smile.

choices.label: Take the deal (£1,500)
choices.result: Twenty-six takes. You can still taste custard in your dreams. The prawns are in there somewhere too.

news.headline: {NAME} GOES CRACKERS FOR PRAWN CUSTARD

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.result: They go with a reality star instead. She's sick in take three. You feel quietly vindicated.

events.text: You scored in the last two games wearing the same pants. You haven't washed them since. Gaz has started getting changed in the corridor.

choices.label: Keep the lucky pants going
choices.result: The pants become a legend. Dennis refuses to touch them without barbecue tongs.

choices.label: Wash them like a normal person
choices.result: You wash them. Nothing terrible happens. You remain deeply suspicious of the washing machine.

events.text: Big Terry insists every player touches the tunnel sign, then pats a framed photo of his late hamster, Gerald. You forgot last week. You lost 4-0. Terry has noticed.

choices.label: Pat Gerald, solemnly
choices.result: Terry nods. 'Gerald approves.' You win 2-1. Nobody can prove anything.

choices.label: Tell Terry it's nonsense
choices.result: Terry doesn't speak to you for a week. Gerald's photo is turned to face away from your peg.

events.text: Mr Pickering here, number 14. Your hedge is over my fence. Also your football came over. Also it beheaded my gnome. Also, for the record, I have a season ticket for the other lot.

choices.label: Trim the hedge yourself (takes your day)
choices.result: You trim it into the shape of the club badge. It looks like a startled hedgehog. He's furious, but impressed.

choices.label: Buy him a new gnome
choices.result: The only gnome in the shop is wearing your club's shirt. He turns it to face the wall.

events.text: Hello love, I've taken in fourteen parcels for you this week. One of them is moving. Another one is ticking. What on earth are you ordering?

choices.label: Pop round with flowers and a signed shirt
choices.result: The moving one was a houseplant with a frog in it. The ticking one was a clock. Mrs Okafor is now your biggest fan.

choices.label: 'Just leave them on the step next time'
choices.result: She does. It rains all week. Your new boots are now a soup.

events.text: A bloke stops you outside the chippy and rolls up his sleeve. He's had your face tattooed on his forearm. It's got a moustache. You don't have a moustache.

choices.label: Sign his arm so he can get it inked
choices.result: He goes straight back to the tattoo parlour. Now he has your face, your autograph and the moustache.

choices.label: Gently ask about the moustache
choices.result: 'Artistic licence,' he says. 'You'll grow into it.'

events.text: A young couple stop you in the park. 'We've named our baby after you!' The baby looks up at you with the deep suspicion of someone who has seen your finishing.

choices.label: Hold the baby for a photo
choices.result: The baby is sick down your shirt. The photo is still lovely. It ends up on the club website.

choices.label: Ask if they're sure
choices.result: 'We weren't until now,' says the dad. 'Now we're not sure at all.'

events.text: The press officer has given you a list of things NOT to talk about. Number four is 'the gaffer's dog'. The first question is about the gaffer's dog.

choices.label: Call the dog 'a great servant to the club'
choices.result: The dog is called Biscuit. By Friday Biscuit has his own fan page. It has more followers than you.

choices.label: Tell the story of the dog eating the team sheet
choices.result: The room is in stitches. The gaffer is not in stitches. Biscuit, for the record, looks guilty.

news.headline: {NAME}: GAFFER'S DOG ATE MY TEAM SELECTION

events.text: The gaffer has bought 600 new training cones. He's colour-coded them. He's named some of them. He wants help laying out a drill he calls 'The Spaghetti Junction'.

choices.label: Help with the cones
choices.result: Two hours. Nobody understands the drill, including the gaffer. He calls it 'his masterpiece'.

choices.label: 'Accidentally' kick a cone into the canal
choices.result: That was Clive. He loved Clive. The lads hold a minute's silence, mostly laughing.

events.text: Son. I've written a song for the team. On the ukulele. Eleven verses, one per player. I need someone to hear it first and be honest. Not too honest.

choices.label: 'It's brilliant, gaffer'
choices.result: He plays it on the team bus for four hours. All eleven verses. Twice. The lads know it was you.

choices.label: Suggest a few changes
choices.result: He sulks for a day, then adds a key change. It's better. Annoyingly, it's much better.

events.text: The gaffer's stuck on 14 down: 'Overpaid show-off who won't track back (7)'. He's not looking at the paper. He's looking at you.

choices.label: 'Striker, gaffer?'
choices.result: He fills it in. Then rubs it out and writes your name. It doesn't fit. He makes it fit.

choices.label: Pretend to tie your laces
choices.result: He gives you 'extra fitness (5,7)'. You don't need to be good at crosswords to solve that one.

events.text: Son, I'm away on a coaching course this weekend. Can you look after Brian? He's a Great Dane. He eats shoes. He's very gentle with them, mind.

choices.label: Dog-sit Brian (takes your day)
choices.result: Brian eats your left boot, a cushion and an entire lasagne. You love him. The gaffer can tell.

choices.label: Recommend a professional dog sitter
choices.result: 'Brian doesn't do strangers,' says the gaffer, in a voice that makes you feel like a stranger.

events.text: The team coach stopped at a motorway services for 'ten minutes'. It's been fifty. The coach driver is in the arcade, glued to the claw machine.

choices.label: Help him win the teddy
choices.result: You win a pink unicorn on the 31st go. It becomes the team's lucky charm. You lose 3-0.

choices.label: Round everyone up
choices.result: You get there on time. The lads call you 'Head Boy' for a month.

events.text: Quick reminder: the warm-weather training camp leaves Monday at 6am. Passports, please. You can't find yours. Mum thinks it's in the airing cupboard. Gran thinks it's 'with the Christmas decorations'.

choices.label: Tear the house apart
choices.result: It was in your boot bag all along. Inside a sock. Inside another sock.

choices.label: Trust Gran's hunch
choices.result: It IS with the Christmas decorations, wrapped in tinsel. Gran will be insufferable about this until next Christmas.

events.text: Your train home is cancelled. The rail replacement bus is a minibus. The minibus is full of a hen party from Wigan. They've recognised you. They have a sash with your name on it already. How?

choices.label: Get on and embrace it
choices.result: You're crowned honorary bridesmaid and made to sing the whole way. You keep the sash. It's in a frame now.

choices.label: Wait for the next one
choices.result: The next one is at 6am. You spend the night on a platform bench next to a pigeon you name Trevor.

events.text: You're making the club nutritionist's 'super easy' recipe. Step one: 'blanch the kale'. You don't know what blanching is. The smoke alarm seems to have a theory.

choices.label: Keep going, you're a chef now
choices.result: It's edible. Just. The kale has gone a colour not found in nature, but it's very nutritious, probably.

choices.label: Give up and order a pizza
choices.result: The pizza man recognises you. 'Does the nutritionist know about this?' He winks. He'll tell her.

events.text: The club's charity bake-off is Friday. Big Terry has been practising a four-foot tower of profiteroles for six weeks. You have Thursday night and a packet of digestives.

choices.label: Go big: a cake shaped like the gaffer's head
choices.result: It slowly collapses in the heat. It still looks a lot like him. That's the problem.

choices.label: Turn up with shop-bought and a straight face
choices.result: You come second. Big Terry weeps into his profiteroles. The judges have questions about your 'family recipe' sticker.

events.text: You've put up a shelf for your trophies. It's at a 30-degree angle. Everything slides off. The neighbour asked if you were building a ski jump.

choices.label: Fix it properly (takes your day)
choices.result: Uncle Ron comes round to inspect it and says 'not bad', the most he has said to anyone since 1997.

choices.label: Call it a 'feature'
choices.result: Your Player of the Month trophy slides off and lands on your toe. You train with a limp and a grudge.

events.text: You watched a video on how to fix a dripping tap. Your kitchen is now a small lido. A duck has turned up. You don't know how the duck got in.

choices.label: Ring a plumber
choices.result: The plumber is a season ticket holder. He charges double 'for that miss on Saturday'. Fair enough.

choices.label: Ring Mum
choices.result: Mum fixes it in four minutes with a butter knife and tells everyone at bingo. The duck stays for tea.

events.text: Barry here, Barry's School of Motoring. Your mum's booked you a taster lesson. I've seen you play, so please check your mirrors more than you check for a pass.

choices.label: Do the taster lesson (takes your day)
choices.result: You stall nine times. On the tenth go you hit 20mph and scream. Barry's twitch gets noticeably worse.

choices.label: Not yet, Barry
choices.result: Barry sounds relieved. Very, very relieved.

events.text: Charity car wash Sunday! The youth team are washing cars for the hospice and they'd love you to bring yours. They have sponges. They have foam. They have very little supervision.

choices.label: Bring your car (and a sponge)
choices.result: Your car comes back gleaming and, somehow, missing a wing mirror. They raise £800. Nobody knows where the mirror went.

choices.label: Just make a donation
choices.result: They send a thank-you card with a drawing of your car. In the drawing it's on fire. Kids.

events.text: You've parked in the gaffer's space. In fairness, it's the only space in the shade. In less fairness, it says GAFFER on it in letters a foot high.

choices.label: Move it before he arrives
choices.result: You move it. He pulls in eight seconds later. He saw. He says nothing. He definitely saw.

choices.label: Leave it and live dangerously
choices.result: He chains his bicycle to your bumper and takes the key home. The lads are thrilled.

events.text: Your new sat nav voice is a very excitable man who shouts 'SMASHING!' at every roundabout. You've followed him to the away ground. The wrong away ground. In Wales.

choices.label: Turn round and get there (legally)
choices.result: You arrive as the warm-up finishes. The gaffer is holding a training cone like a weapon.

choices.label: Ring the gaffer and confess
choices.result: He sends Dennis in the kit van to fetch you. Dennis plays panpipes the whole way back. 'SMASHING,' says the sat nav.

events.text: It's 2am in town. The lads want to carry on to a nightclub called Inferno. You've got recovery at 9. Gaz is already doing the worm in the taxi queue.

choices.label: On to Inferno
choices.result: The dance floor is sticky enough to hold you upright. You get home at five. Recovery is a rumour.

choices.label: Get chips and go home
choices.result: The chips are perfect. The lads send you 70 videos, which you watch over breakfast feeling smug.

events.text: STAG DO IN RIGA BROS!!! 3 days. matching t-shirts with my face on. the gaffer said 'over my dead body' but he says that about everything

choices.label: Go to Riga (takes your day)
choices.result: You come back with one eyebrow and no memory of a tank. There was definitely a tank. There are photos of the tank.

news.headline: TANK YOU VERY MUCH: {NAME}'S STAG DO EYEBROW SHAME

choices.label: Stay home, send a card
choices.result: Kev reads your card out at the wedding. It says 'Congratulations on your retirement'. Wrong card.

events.text: The club sponsor's charity 'Casino Night'. Black tie. Fake money, real roulette wheel. Big Terry has already lost his fake house and is trying to win back his fake dog.

choices.label: Hit the tables (for charity)
choices.result: You win a fortune in fake money and spend it all on a fake yacht. The hospice gets a very real £12,000.

choices.label: Guard the buffet
choices.result: You eat 40 vol-au-vents. It's a club record. Big Terry tries to wager his fake dog on you beating it.

events.text: An office Christmas party has spotted you at the bar. A woman called Linda is holding out a microphone like a sword. The song is a nine-minute power ballad.

choices.label: Duet with Linda
choices.result: You do the deep bits. Linda does everything else, including a knee slide. Standing ovation.

choices.label: Run
choices.result: You run. Linda chases you three streets in heels. She's quick, is Linda. She gets the duet in the end.

events.text: Derby week. Their striker has posted a photo of himself wiping his feet on a doormat with your club's badge on it. The internet is waiting for your reply.

choices.label: Reply with a doormat that has HIS face on it
choices.result: Your doormat sells 5,000 units by Friday. The FA would like a quiet word.

news.headline: WELCOME MAT-TER: {NAME} HITS BACK IN DERBY DOORMAT ROW

choices.label: Just reply 'see you Saturday'
choices.result: Three words. Ice cold. You practise saying them in the mirror for an hour.

events.text: Love, Graham's coming to Sunday lunch. Yes, he supports the other lot. Yes, he's wearing the shirt. It's derby week, I know. Please be nice. x

choices.label: Be nice (takes your day)
choices.result: You pass the gravy. He passes the gravy. A fragile peace holds until the crumble.

choices.label: Turn up in full kit with a vuvuzela
choices.result: Mum doesn't speak to you until Tuesday. Graham secretly asks for a selfie on the way out.

events.text: After your miss on Saturday, someone has renamed the squad group chat 'Row Z Appreciation Society'. It has a new profile picture. It's the ball, still in the air.

choices.label: Rename it something worse about Gaz
choices.result: The chat is renamed fourteen times before lunch. The gaffer leaves the group. Then rejoins to vote.

choices.label: Mute it for a week
choices.result: You miss 900 messages, a fines vote and the news that Kev's having twins.

events.text: You're in charge of the pre-match playlist. Big Terry wants 80s power ballads. The young lads want drill. The gaffer wants 'something with a brass section'.

choices.label: Power ballads
choices.result: Big Terry warms up doing air guitar. Your full-back pulls a hamstring doing air drums. You win anyway.

choices.label: Drill
choices.result: The gaffer stands in the corner with his fingers in his ears, doing his crossword.

choices.label: Brass band versions of everything
choices.result: A brass band cover of a grime track. Nobody knows how to feel. The gaffer has tears in his eyes.

events.text: A flock of pigeons has taken over the training pitch. The groundsman says they're 'protected'. They're not protected. He just likes them. He's named them.

choices.label: Train around them
choices.result: You nutmeg a pigeon. It's the best bit of skill you've done all season, and nobody filmed it.

choices.label: Pay for a hawk
choices.result: The hawk takes one look at the pigeons and flies off towards the M6. The groundsman is delighted.

events.text: The pitch sprinklers come on halfway through the gaffer's team talk. He keeps talking. He refuses to acknowledge them. Everyone is soaked.

choices.label: Stand there and listen, dripping
choices.result: '...and THAT is why we press high,' he finishes. Nobody heard a word. Total respect.

choices.label: Run for cover
choices.result: Half the squad follows you. The gaffer finishes his talk to the cones, who listen beautifully.

events.text: The new signing doesn't speak much English yet. His only phrase so far is 'Where is the toaster?' The gaffer asks you to show him round.

choices.label: Take him under your wing (takes your day)
choices.result: You show him the toaster. He cries. It's a long story involving his gran. You're best mates now.

choices.label: Teach him rude words instead
choices.result: He uses every one of them at his first press conference. Beautifully pronounced.

news.headline: NEW BOY'S BLUE PRESSER: {NAME} BLAMED FOR LANGUAGE LESSONS

events.text: It's Dennis's 70th birthday today. Nobody knows. Dennis knows. Dennis has mentioned it to you four times this morning, completely unprompted.

choices.label: Organise a surprise for Dennis
choices.result: The whole squad sings. Dennis cries, then grips your arm: 'Beware a man holding a clipboard.' Then he cuts the cake.

choices.label: Grab him a card from the garage
choices.result: It's a card for a new baby boy. Dennis puts it on his shelf anyway, facing out.

events.text: Dennis has ironed your shirt number on upside down. Your 9 is now a 6. He says it isn't a mistake. He says it's 'a message'.

choices.label: Wear it and trust Dennis
choices.result: You score twice. Dennis just nods from the tunnel, like he knew. He did know.

choices.label: Ask for a new shirt
choices.result: Dennis hands it over with a look that will haunt you until the end of the season.

events.text: Our main sponsor, Pringleton Windows, is holding its annual awards. They'd love a player to present 'Double Glazer of the Year'. It's a big deal in double glazing.

choices.label: Present the award (takes your day)
choices.result: The winner, Clive, thanks you, his mum and his squeegee, in that order. It's genuinely moving.

choices.label: Make an excuse
choices.result: They ask Barry the Badger instead. Neville gives a twenty-minute speech about mascot rights.

events.text: Hi! We're doing a feature on footballers' skincare routines. What's yours? (You use the same shower gel for your face, your hair, your legs and your boots.)

choices.label: Invent an elaborate routine
choices.result: You say 'avocado' eleven times. Avocado sales in the town go up 12%. Your face does not change.

choices.label: Tell the truth
choices.result: Readers find it refreshing. A shower gel company sends you a crate, out of pity.

news.headline: SOAP-ER STAR: {NAME}'S ONE-BOTTLE BEAUTY SECRET

events.text: A letter from a 9-year-old called Ellie. You're her favourite player, she says, but her second favourite is a Labrador called Duke, and 'it is very close'.

choices.label: Write back with a signed photo
choices.result: Ellie writes again. You've pulled ahead of Duke. Duke's family are said to be furious.

choices.label: Send a photo of you with a borrowed Labrador
choices.result: The Labrador licks your face for the whole shoot. Ellie declares it a draw. Diplomacy.

events.text: Good news! I've signed you up for the charity 10k on Sunday. You're running it dressed as a banana. Bad news: the banana costume is a size small.

choices.label: Run as the banana (takes your day)
choices.result: You finish 212th, just behind a man dressed as a fridge. You raise £3,500 and chafe in new places.

choices.label: Pull a fake hamstring
choices.result: A photographer catches you jogging to the shop on Monday, perfectly fine.

news.headline: BANANA SPLIT: {NAME} SLIPS OUT OF CHARITY RUN

events.text: Three lads at the bus stop recognise you. 'Do the celebration!' they shout. You don't have a celebration. They're expecting one anyway.

choices.label: Invent one on the spot
choices.result: You do a sort of crab walk into a salute. Within a week every kid in town is doing it. You have to do it now. Forever.

choices.label: 'I'm saving it for Saturday'
choices.result: Mysterious. Cool. Now you need a celebration by Saturday. You practise in the kitchen. The cat watches.

events.text: A lovely old man asks you to sign his shirt. You do. He looks at it, then at you, then says 'You're not the goalkeeper.' He's been looking for the goalkeeper.

choices.label: Take him to meet the goalkeeper
choices.result: The keeper signs right next to your name. The old man frames it. You're both in his downstairs loo now. An honour.

choices.label: Insist you could play in goal
choices.result: He makes you prove it in the park. You let in seven against a man of 84.

events.text: The club chef has 'refreshed' the training ground breakfast. The bacon has gone. In its place is something called a 'chia pudding'. It's looking at you.

choices.label: Lead a bacon rebellion
choices.result: You hold a sit-in by the toaster. The bacon returns on Fridays only. History will call it the Bacon Accord.

choices.label: Eat the chia pudding
choices.result: It's a bit like frogspawn. You feel incredible. You'll never admit it.

events.text: Radio Bantam's 'Quick-Fire Friday'! Ten questions in sixty seconds. Question one: if the gaffer were a sandwich, what sandwich would he be?

choices.label: 'A big, honest cheese and pickle'
choices.result: The gaffer has 'Cheese and Pickle' put on the back of his training top. He's never been happier.

choices.label: 'A soggy egg one left on a radiator'
choices.result: The listeners love it. The gaffer leaves an egg sandwich on your peg every day for a fortnight.

news.headline: EGG ON HIS FACE: {NAME}'S SANDWICH SLUR ON GAFFER

events.text: Dear former pupil. Mrs Abernathy (Geography) is retiring after 41 years. She has asked if you'd come and say a few words. She would also like her protractor back. She knows you have it.

choices.label: Go and give a speech, protractor in hand (takes your day)
choices.result: You return the protractor to a standing ovation. Mrs Abernathy says you were 'a lovely boy with no sense of direction'. Fair.

choices.label: Post the protractor back with a card
choices.result: She writes back to say the card's lovely but you've spelt 'geography' wrong. Twice.
